questions.title: What is your total budget for the entire trip?
questions.description: Budget determines which accommodations, restaurants, and activities are realistic.

questions.title: Are you traveling solo, with a couple, or with a family?
questions.description: The group size affects the itinerary's scale, dining choices, and activity options.

questions.title: Do you have a specific timeframe in mind for the trip?
questions.description: The travel window helps identify available flight deals and seasonal considerations.

questions.title: Are you a first-time visitor or a repeat traveler?
questions.description: Knowing whether this is a first visit or a return trip shapes which must-see landmarks to include.

questions.title: Do you have any mobility limitations or physical needs?
questions.description: Physical constraints affect which landmarks, museums, and activities are accessible.

questions.title: Is there a specific experience you want to prioritize?
questions.description: The user may want a romantic dinner, a luxury shopping spree, a food tour, or a cultural museum visit.

input: Plan a trip to Paris

verdict.notes: Set B misses two critical logistics questions — departure city (needed for flights/transport) and accommodation preference — which are essential for planning a trip. Question 3 also slightly combines multiple traveler types in one ask, and "first-time vs. repeat visitor" while useful is less critical than the missing logistics gaps.

questions.title: What is your total budget for this garden?
questions.description: Understanding the budget helps determine whether to focus on seeds, plants, tools, or a mix of all three.

questions.title: What is the size of your available growing space?
questions.description: The size of the garden determines whether to plan for a small balcony, a backyard, or a community plot.

questions.title: What is your experience level with gardening?
questions.description: The user's experience level shapes which plants to choose, how to set up the garden, and how to manage it.

questions.title: What types of vegetables are you most interested in?
questions.description: Knowing the user's preferences helps narrow down which plants to grow and what varieties to select.

questions.title: Do you have a specific climate or region in mind?
questions.description: The local climate affects which plants are suitable, how to prepare the soil, and when to plant.

questions.title: Is this garden for personal use or a specific purpose?
questions.description: The intended use, such as a restaurant supply chain, a family garden, or a community project, affects the scale and goals of the garden.

questions.title: When do you want to start the growing season?
questions.description: The target start date determines the planting timeline and whether to plan for a spring, summer, or fall garden.
